question: Which of the following animals is listed as endangered and protected under the Indian Wildlife Protection Act, 1972?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lion-tailed macaque**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lion-tailed macaque**, also known as the **Wanderoo**, is an **endangered species** listed under the Indian Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
 
• It is endemic to the **Western Ghats** of India, particularly in states like **Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The species resides in **rainforests** and prefers dense, evergreen forests at elevations ranging from **600 to 1,800 meters**.
 
• The Lion-tailed macaque is characterized by its **black fur** and a distinctive **silver-white mane** that surrounds its face, resembling a lion.
 
• It is primarily **arboreal**, spending most of its time in the trees and is known for being an excellent climber.
 
• Its diet consists mainly of **fruits, leaves, insects, and small animals**, making it an important contributor to the forest ecosystem.
 
• The species faces threats due to **habitat loss** caused by deforestation, agriculture, and human encroachment.
 
• Conservation efforts for the Lion-tailed macaque include **protected reserves** like the Silent Valley National Park and other wildlife sanctuaries in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is recognized as **Endangered** by the **IUCN Red List**, emphasizing the need for its protection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hanuman Langur**__

 __
 
• The **Hanuman Langur** is one of the most commonly found species of monkeys in India.
 
• It is named after the Hindu deity **Hanuman**, who is often depicted as a monkey.
 
• They are not considered endangered and are widespread across **India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka**.
 
• Hanuman Langurs are known for their ability to adapt to various habitats, including forests, grasslands, and even urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Peacock**__
 __
 
• The **Indian Peafowl**, commonly known as the Peacock, is India's **National Bird**.
 
• Peacocks are known for their **iridescent feathers** and elaborate displays during courtship.
 
• They are protected under the **Indian Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, but they are not considered endangered.
 
• Peacocks are found in forests, agricultural lands, and even human settlements across **India and South Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Nilgai**__
 
 
• The **Nilgai**, also known as the Blue Bull, is the **largest antelope** in India.
 
• It is native to the Indian subcontinent and is found in **open grasslands and woodlands**.
 
• Nilgais are not considered endangered and are frequently seen in protected areas and agricultural lands.
 
• They are herbivores and primarily feed on grasses, leaves, and fruits.
